per_reference_rules.rule: D0018 model-fix list item 1 (T0317): E008's design rules of a reference are drc.rules.measure_rules on the snapped reconstruction with min_signal_wire_length set to None (the measured minimum gate/Kelvin-wire length, which measure_rules sets to the reference's shortest signal wire, src/moduleforge/drc/rules.py line 587). Every upper bound (max_gate_wire_length, max_kelvin_wire_length, max_signal_wire_length) and every other measured rule is kept. One runner function builds them, e008_run.e008_rules, and writes info.rules_record (the dropped field, the value measure_rules gave it, the upper bounds kept, the fields changed). Every place the runner builds a reference or dev spec uses it (dev_reference: 2D_Case_4 from measure_rules plus its dev overrides; generator housing layouts from their generator spec's rules, where the field is already None); the judged-reference loader judged_reference (T0320, D0019) uses it with no override, and prepare() refuses any spec without its rules_record or with min_signal_wire_length set (review T0319 finding 0). The twin, D (through d_spec) and every main and control candidate get the reference's spec built from these rules, so the candidates lose the lower bound too.
per_reference_rules.basis: D0018 (project/decisions/D0018-o003-e008-degraded-copy-yardstick.md, model-fix list item 1, fixed before any candidate reference was screened) reads O003 scope_in's enumerated rules as the complete meaning of "design rules at least as strict as the reference's own"; the scope_in bondability rule bounds gate and Kelvin wires from above only (project/objectives/O003/objective.yaml lines 61-63; review T0315 finding 2, which flagged this as an interpretation for the founder). T0314 (research/notes/o003-twin-coverage.md section 1, variant R1) found this lower bound to be the only rule that stops a twin whose gate wires run to the nearest gate copper (2D_Case_2R: twin LS gate wires 4.597 mm against the reference's 5.344-10.396 mm).

config.degrade_power_width_floor_reason: D0018 decision 1 (T0316). D is a yardstick: it sets only L_sub(D), its band solves and w_ctrl = 2 e_R(control best, D); the control candidates come from the reference's spec (search.run_control). So D's power-net copper (DC+, PHASE, DC-) may be narrower than the reference's own minimum power-net width, down to this floor: degrade() gets the reference's spec with min_width_power = min(reference minimum, floor) (e008_run.d_spec); every other rule applies to D unchanged; W, the candidates and both searches keep the reference's rules. Why 1.5 mm, the smallest floor the evidence supports: (a) the generator's default minimum width is 1.0 mm (DesignRules.min_trace_width); (b) at 1.0 mm D's narrowest strip has 2 cells across at the band solves' 0.5 mm levels (4 of the 5 levels), both edge cells, where the 20 MHz current crowds; at 1.5 mm it has 3 (one interior cell) and 6 at 0.25 mm. The lateral term of e_R(control best, D) on such strips could not be measured within T0316's limits (no 0.25 mm solve; a 1.0 mm level cannot run on 0.5 mm-grid layouts), so excluding 1.0 mm rests on this resolution argument (inference); the 0.5 mm thickness-term check is in research/o003/e008_dev/d_floor/l2_strip_check_gen2x1_w2_s11.json; (c) L0/L1 (research/o003/e008_dev/d_floor/floor_study.json, 2D_Case_4 and 7 generator housing layouts with 2-5 mm power rules): D reaches the L1 target 1.3875 on 8/8 at 1.0 mm, 7/8 at 1.5 mm, 6/8 at 2.0 mm and 3/8 at the reference minimum; on 2D_Case_4 1.421 (1.0 mm), 1.391 (1.5 mm: narrow_landing and 7 walk steps), 1.390 (2.0 mm), 1.232 (5 mm, DegradeError). Frozen: --verify-freeze checks this value against the runner constant DEGRADE_POWER_WIDTH_FLOOR_M and that it is >= 1 mm

reporting.virtual_junction: D0020 item 2 (T0330): REPORTED, NOT GATED. Die-average Tj ('virtual junction temperature'): per die and scikit-fem level, T_vj = (1/A) * integral over the die top face of T dA, the area-weighted mean of the FE solution over the die's top face (the heat-source face, A = the die footprint), as thermal_fem computes ThermalResult.tj_mean: the facet load vector of the top face (FacetBasis, intorder 4) restricted to the face DOFs and divided by its sum A (checked against the footprint to 1e-6), dotted with the nodal temperatures (the method of T0325's tj_osc.py). Die-row columns Tvj_l0_K, Tvj_l1_K, Tvj_l2_K and GCI_vj_K = gci_capped(levels 0-2, floor 1e-3 K); the evaluation report's 'virtual_junction' section (labelled as not the registered criterion) gives per reference and layout tj_bounds on T_vj, per thermally checked candidate the conservative-test analogue upper_vj(C) - lower_vj(W) against 2 K, and the h_lo that A1's formula (mfos.metrics.headroom_per_reference, unchanged) gives when every die row of that reference carries T_vj in place of Tj max (so F1(a2) is then read on T_vj too). No gated metric, sanity check, stop rule or F3 order reads it: mfos.metrics reads only Tj_l0..2_K and the frozen search keeps only its THERMAL_REQUIRED fields. The solve's physics inputs and result-file key are unchanged (the dev rows were replayed with no solve started); development results solved before T0330 carry null for it. Selftest: a uniform die gives its own temperature (zero-power solves at two coolant temperatures), mean <= max on every die (real solves and T0325's level-2 data), and mutation: NaN, +/-100 K, null or absent columns change no gated metric, check or report value, with a positive control. T0332: h_lo_vj is made computable on a real run. After the frozen driver has finished and the gated rows are assembled, per reference the runner determines the 'die-average best': the layout A1's formula (mfos.metrics.headroom_per_reference, unchanged) picks on virtual_junction_report's row copy with T_vj in place of Tj max (vj_best_layouts; no exception text is parsed: a layout without band columns gets placeholder values in a probe copy, which cannot change best_id because the formula reads the band only for e_R after best is fixed). If that layout's row lacks the band columns (L_sub_c05_H, L_sub_thk_c_H, L_sub_thk_f_H, L_sub_wire_f_H), its BAND em_jobs are submitted through its reference's main Driver and the run's Scheduler (same job keys and solver settings as every other band solve, so a resumed run finds them; phase A/B split as any job), only after every gated solve is done; their values go into the report's own row copy only, never into the gated rows, er.rows, the metrics, the checks, the stop rules or the F3 order. The report then gives h_lo_vj with best_id_vj and die_average_best (layout, fingerprint, the Tj-max and inductance-only bests for the record, band_source 'solved for this report only' or 'gated rows', new_solves). Any failure (solver error, memory, phase stop) or --replay-only with a missing band leaves h_lo_vj null with h_lo_vj_reason; it never raises and changes no gated value. --plan prices at most one band set per counted reference (cost_estimate.vj_band_extra). Selftest (vj_band_failures): a synthetic case whose die-average best differs from the Tj-max best and the inductance-only best and has no band in the gated rows: h_lo_vj non-null and equal to headroom_per_reference on the T_vj copy carrying that band; rows, metrics, checks and the gated report byte-identical with the step disabled; resume solves nothing; --replay-only and a planted failing band job give null with a reason and change nothing gated

twin_limitations: rectangular merged bands are split by the midpoint-of-needs convention; the copper does not fix the boundary (T0297)
a column that fills the gap beside the narrower slot leaves no step, so the tie rule decides the split (T0300)
a neck from below or above that covers a slot's probe u enters the band's v-interval and counts as band copper, so the split can be wrong end to end (T0302 finding 0)
copper is assumed axis-parallel (non-rectilinear copper is staircased by the snapping rule first)
